title: Lesson 8: How to Disciple Others
description: Someone once helped you follow Jesus. This lesson shows how to walk alongside your one, or anyone ready to grow, the way Jesus walked with His disciples, so that the blessing you received keeps being passed on.

blocks.text: In Lessons 2 through 5 you learned to BLESS your one: begin with prayer, listen, eat, serve, and story. Then you carried that rhythm into work and school and learned to stand firm in the battle. When your one says yes to Jesus, SPACES is how you walk with them. This lesson shows how to sit down with someone as they follow Jesus, then send them to help someone else.

blocks.alt: An older Paul works with his hands on tent cloth and rope while a young Timothy sits close beside him, listening

blocks.title: Four Generations
blocks.text:
When Paul met Timothy in Lystra, Timothy was already a disciple with a good reputation among the believers (Acts 16:1-2). Paul invited him to travel and serve alongside him. Timothy heard Paul teach and watched how he lived through hardship. Years later Paul reminded him, "You, however, have followed my teaching, my conduct, my aim in life, my faith, my patience, my love, my steadfastness" (2 Timothy 3:10).

Paul did more than give Timothy information. He shared his life and prepared Timothy to lead. Then Paul gave Timothy a charge that reached far beyond the two of them.
and what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.

That verse holds four generations: Paul, Timothy, faithful people, and others. Paul sat with Timothy, then sent him to sit with others. Someone has done that for you too, opening the Bible with you, praying for you, and believing God was at work in you. You are blessed to be a blessing, and that includes passing on what you were given.
8.1 - Who has helped you grow in love for God and others? What did that person do?
Jesus Calls Ordinary People to Make Disciples

Jesus chose twelve disciples "so that they might be with him and he might send them out to preach" (Mark 3:14). They heard His teaching, watched His compassion for people, and practiced His way, and when they came back from serving He listened to all they had done (Mark 6:30). After His resurrection He told them to make disciples of all nations, "teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you" (Matthew 28:19-20). That includes this command too, so every disciple is meant to become a disciple-maker.
The goal was never just more Bible facts. Discipleship helps a person grow in love for God and others and learn to obey Jesus in everyday life.

You may feel unqualified because you still have questions and still struggle with sin, but so did the people Jesus first called. You do not need to be a perfect Christian or have every answer. You just need to keep following Jesus, care about another person, and share what you are learning. And you will not do it alone. Jesus ends the Great Commission with a promise: "I am with you always" (Matthew 28:20).
Sit Down Together

Discipleship grows when people sit down together, whether it is one friend over coffee or a few around a table in your small group. There is room to ask honest questions, face struggles, practice obeying Jesus, and celebrate progress. Watch what happens at one table.
Make SPACES

Did you see the word take shape? Make SPACES: Study, Practice, Appropriate Challenge, Encourage, Send. Each step has one word to hold onto: study to learn, practice to talk, give an appropriate challenge to do, encourage to keep on, and send so others will go. Jesus did every one of these with His disciples, and by His grace you can do them with someone else.

blocks.title: SPACES at Your Table
content: Study: Learn. Open God's Word together, starting with the Growing Together lessons that fit the person. The goal is not to finish pages but to help someone know Jesus and love Him more.

Practice: Talk. Faith grows stronger when it is put into words. Practice praying, explaining a passage, or telling how you came to follow Jesus. You might say, "Let's practice sharing your testimony. You can share yours with me first."

Appropriate Challenge: Do. Knowing is not the same as doing (Matthew 7:24). With hopeful eyes, say something like, "I see in you a heart for people. I want to challenge you to start a conversation about Jesus with someone this week." A good challenge stretches someone without leaving them on their own.

Encourage: Keep On. Ask what happened, listen, pray, and celebrate the courage it took to try. If it did not go well, stay close and help them choose another step. Paul kept strengthening Timothy through his letters long after they were apart.

Send: Go. Jesus said, "As the Father has sent me, even so I am sending you" (John 20:21). You might say, "You are ready to sit down with someone else. Would you invite one person to begin Growing Together with you?" Then keep cheering them on as they go.

blocks.text: 8.2 - Think about the person who helped you grow. Which of these five did they do with you: learn, talk, do, keep on, or go? Which one do you most want to pass on to someone else?
Addition or Multiplication

When one person helps another grow in Jesus, that is worth celebrating every time. But Paul asked Timothy for more: faithful people "who will be able to teach others also." If you helped one person grow in Jesus every year by yourself, in ten years you would have walked with ten people, and that is a life well spent. But if you disciple one person this year, and next year each of you disciples one more, and everyone keeps going, in ten years there would be more than a thousand disciple-makers. Addition gathers people around you. Multiplication sends people out from you, and it keeps growing long after you.

Multiplication does not happen through information alone. Paul and Timothy wrote to a young church, "we were ready to share with you not only the gospel of God but also our own selves, because you had become very dear to us" (1 Thessalonians 2:8). That is life-on-life ministry: truth and love shared around the same table. And it changes you too. Going through a study the first time is like tasting great food. Leading someone else through it is like chewing it up and consuming it, so that it becomes part of you.
Your Appropriate Challenge

So where do you start? Invite one person, or a few, to go through Growing Together with you. It might be your one, if they have said yes to Jesus, or someone in your church who is ready to grow. Look for someone who is faithful, available, and teachable. They do not need to know much or look impressive. Meet once a week or every other week, open a lesson, and walk SPACES together.

If you are going through this lesson with someone right now, look across the table. This may be your appropriate challenge: it is time to be sent. You have tasted the food, and now you get to serve it to someone else, with the person who discipled you promising, "I will be here to help and encourage you all along the way."
8.3 - Who is one faithful, available, and teachable person you could invite to go through Growing Together with you? Write down their name and when you could ask them.
God Gives the Growth

Think of an orchard. A gardener can prepare the soil, plant, and water a young tree, but the gardener cannot make it live. "I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth" (1 Corinthians 3:6). Changing a heart is God's work, not yours. Your part is to make space, open His Word, walk with them, and depend on the Holy Spirit. Some conversations will feel fruitful and others slow, so keep praying and keep caring.
8.4 - Dream for a moment. If the person you named one day disciples someone else, and that person does the same, what might God do through your one yes in the next five years?
Lesson 8 Review

Paul poured his life into Timothy, and Timothy passed it on to faithful people who would teach others also. When your one says yes to Jesus, SPACES is how you walk with them: study to learn, practice to talk, give an appropriate challenge to do, encourage to keep on, and send so others will go. You are blessed to be a blessing. Make space for one person and send them to do the same, and the worship of God grows one table at a time. And Jesus is with you always.
In the next lesson, you will see who God puts beside you in His mission, as the blessing moves from your city to every nation.
Closing Reflections
